title: Customer postmortem briefing + verification checklist (one-pager)
content:
TL;DR
On 2026-11-01 09:12 UTC we observed elevated tail latency and truncated structured outputs for requests routed to the EU inference pool. Impact window ~09:12–09:57 UTC (≈45 minutes). Root cause: a canary rollout of a routing mesh update introduced an encoding mismatch for prefix/KV cache keys between old and new router binaries, causing widespread cache misses, increased queuing, and occasional stream truncation for a subset of tenants.

What customers saw
- Increased 95/99th percentile latency for text generation and streaming sessions in eu-west-1.
- Some structured outputs (JSON/serialized tool-call responses) were truncated or cut mid-response for affected sessions.
- Errors were transient; successful requests resumed after the rollback.

Immediate mitigation performed (what we did)
1) Rolled the routing mesh canary back to the previous stable version at 09:20 UTC.
2) Enabled emergency routing policy to route traffic away from the small canary wave while we verified caches.
3) Flushed inter-node prefix/KV caches in affected clusters to remove inconsistent keys (09:25–09:35 UTC).
4) Temporarily increased worker concurrency in eu-west-1 to drain queues faster and reduce tail latency.
5) Replayed internal test prompts and a customer-provided probe set; validated structured-output integrity at ~09:54 UTC.

Verified customer-facing resolution
- By 09:57 UTC normal request latency and structured-output behavior had returned for all sampled tenants.
- No data loss detected; partial/truncated responses were transient and limited to in-flight sessions during the window.

Root cause (concise)
A change to the routing mesh altered how prefix and KV cache keys were serialized (different utf-8 escaping and a field order change). The new binary landed in a canary group while other nodes still used the old encoding. When requests were routed across mismatch binaries, cache lookups failed, generating cache-miss cascades that increased CPU and queueing on model workers and occasionally triggered stream termination in the streaming proxy. The code change passed unit tests but was not covered by existing cross-version integration tests.

Customer impact and scope
- Affected region: eu-west-1 only.
- Affected tenants: ~3.2% of active tenants during the window (those routed through canary nodes).
- No persisted customer data corruption found.
- Some customers may have observed truncated outputs and higher latency for in-flight calls; retrying the requests after the incident produced normal responses.

Recommended customer actions (simple, optional)
- If you observed truncated/partial structured responses, retry the same request once; the retry should return a complete response.
- For streaming clients: add logic to detect mid-stream truncation (missing terminal token or out-of-band length header) and retry or fail-safe to a non-streaming response path.
- Optionally pin critical routes to a specific model+runtime version in the Redwood API while we complete the permanent fix — contact us if you need help.

Verification checklist (for customers who want to confirm)
1) Reproduce a quick request and check headers: curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" \\n   "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" --data '{"model":"<model>","input":"ping"}'
   - Confirm X-Req-Id returned and status 200.
2) For streaming: open a stream and verify you receive a full terminal token (e.g., "[DONE]" or the expected JSON close).
3) If you keep logs, search for requests in the 09:10–10:05 UTC window for elevated latency or truncated payloads and include X-Req-Id when contacting support.
4) If you use prefix/KV caching on your side, confirm that you are not relying on cross-node shared cache semantics (server-side caches are the source of the issue).

Compensation and SLA notes
- We will apply a service credit pro-rated to the impacted usage window to customers who experienced measurable SLA violations. Our support team will reach out with a tailored credit calculation for accounts tagged as impacted.

Planned follow-ups (what we will do next)
- Deploy a compatibility shim and strict serialization contract tests to prevent cross-version cache-key mismatches (ETA: 2026-11-10).
- Add cross-version integration tests into the canary gating pipeline (ETA: 2026-11-05).
- Improve streaming proxy resiliency to avoid mid-stream terminations during routing anomalies (ETA: 2026-11-17).
- Provide a short runbook for tenants on pinning routes and detecting truncated streams; Customer Success will offer 1:1 assistance for enterprise tenants.

Owner & contacts
- Primary cust. success contact: Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.ai) — customer liaison and credit coordination.
- SRE lead: Diego Morales (oncall escalation) — diego@redwood.ai.
- Engineering owner for fix: Priya Nair (priya@redwood.ai).

FAQ (short)
Q: Will my data be replayed or reprocessed as a result of the rollback?
A: No automated reprocessing occurred. We did not re-run customer inference workloads unless explicitly requested for debugging. If you want us to re-run a request set, contact support and provide request IDs/timestamps.

Q: Did this affect embeddings or stored model artifacts?
A: No — stored model artifacts and embedding indices were not touched. The issue was in routing/cache lookup semantics only.

Q: How can I avoid impact for future canaries?
A: We recommend pinning critical production routes during our scheduled mesh upgrades (CS can assist). We will also improve our testing and gating to reduce this class of regressions.

Document notes and provenance
- This is a one-page customer-facing summary derived from the internal incident timeline and postmortem draft (see linked Confluence/Jira).
- Status: awaiting engineering confirmation of the permanent fix timeline (in_review).

If you want a shorter status update for posting to your status page, reply and we will provide a 2–3 sentence blurb suitable for public status.redwood.ai.
